result:
I wrote `<out>/run-1/run/classification.toml`, and `gen_schema.py` accepted it (no output, no errors).

**Public values (logged as is):**
- `username` and the token `name` are labelled `public`. R7.2 wants the username and token name in the log.
- `minutes` on `tick` is a `u64`.

**Secret kinds:**

| Kind | Views | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `eq`, `check`, `len`, `keyed_hash`, deliver | `eq` looks up identities and matches verify/recover codes. `check` and `len` cover the format and 254-character rules (R2.2). `keyed_hash` lets operators tell whether events concern the same address without logging it (R7.3). `deliver` is for `whoami` and `outbox` output. |
| `login_identifier` | `eq_public`, `eq_with:email`, `known_identifier` | It can be a mistyped password. `eq_public` matches it against usernames, `eq_with:email` against emails (R4.1). `known_identifier` allows logging it only when it matches an existing identity (R7.4). |
| `password` | `check`, `password_hash` | `check` enforces 12–128 characters (R2.2). `password_hash` covers salted storage and verification (R2.3). Login and `new_password` share this kind. No `deliver`. |
| `verification_code` | `eq`, `check`, `digest`, deliver, `generate = digits:6` | `eq` compares the submitted code with the stored one. `digest` is for storage (R3). `deliver` puts it in the outbox. |
| `recovery_code` | `eq`, `check`, `digest`, deliver, `generate = digits:6` | Same as above (R5). I kept it separate from the verification code so one kind of code can't be swapped for the other. |
| `session_token` | `eq`, `digest`, deliver, `generate = hex:64` | 32 random bytes as hex (R4.2). `eq` looks up the session. `digest` is for storage. `deliver` lets `login` print it. |
| `access_token` | `eq`, `check`, `digest`, `last_n:8`, deliver, `generate = hex:40` | 40 hex characters (R6.1). `last_n:8` serves `token-list` and the audit entry (R6.3, R7.2). `digest` stores only a hash (R6.2). `deliver` shows it once on `token-create`. |

All 14 commands from the requirements are listed with their arguments in order.
